paper_title: NExtLong Toward Effective Long-Context Training without Long Documents
caption: NExtLong reduces the model's dependence on proximal text. We calculated the degree of dependence on proximal text (the last third of the text) for different methods when completing the LongQA task. It can be observed that NExtLong significantly reduces the model's dependence on proximal text.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the attention weight associated with short-dependence for several methods, specifically in relation to the LongQA task. The horizontal axis displays the methods, labeled as Standard, ICLM, KNN, Quest, and NExtLong, listed in that order from left to right. The vertical axis is labeled "Attention Weight," with a linear scale ranging from 0.80 to 0.90, and tick labels at intervals of 0.02. The bars representing each method are all colored in a light blue. The shortest bar, corresponding to NExtLong, has an approximate attention weight of 0.82, while the tallest bar, corresponding to Standard, has an approximate attention weight of 0.88. The values generally decrease then increase again from left to right, with a mid-point around Quest, before decreasing again, though the variations are slight and the values are close to each other. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or outlining, and the bars are sorted alphabetically by method name.
